item.research_question: Can a Ni-Co-Fe-Cr-Al-Ti high-entropy alloy be manufactured via Directed Energy Deposition (DED) to achieve a γ + γ′ phase structure that enhances thermal stability, coarsening resistance, and strength compared to typical FCC-structured HEAs?
item.material_system: Ni-Co-Fe-Cr-Al-Ti HEA (45.0 at% Ni, 20.0 at% Co, 10.0 at% Fe, 10.0 at% Cr, 7.5 at% Al, 7.5 at% Ti) deposited on SUS 304 substrates
item.processing_route: Direct Energy Deposition (DED) using a 2 kW diode laser (980 nm, 3 mm beam diameter) with a laser velocity of 10 mm/s, powder feed rate of 7 g/min, hatch spacing of 1 mm, and 11 layers; powders (45 and 150 μm) mixed for 4 hours; nitrogen carrier gas used to prevent oxidation
item.test_conditions: Room temperature (20 °C) tensile testing per ASTM E8/E8M-18 standard on specimens with 4.5 mm thickness; microhardness measured via Vickers tester with 5 readings per height; XRD (Cu radiation, 40 kV, 50 mA) and EBSD analysis performed
key_findings: The alloy exhibited a γ + γ′ phase structure with an ordered FCC (L12) γ′ phase confirmed by XRD superlattice peaks.
Yield strength was measured at 514 MPa and ultimate tensile strength at 605 MPa (631 MPa in conclusions).
Microhardness was consistent at approximately 370 HV across the deposited height.
The average grain size of the γ phase was coarse, measured at 116 μm.
The γ′ phase composition was identified as (Ni, Co)3(Ti, Al) via EDS analysis.
No secondary precipitated phases other than γ + γ′ were detected in the microstructure.
The hardness exceeded that of wrought Inconel 718 (350 HV).
item.mechanism: The addition of aluminum and titanium creates a γ + γ′ phase structure within the multicomponent FCC-HEA matrix, where the ordered FCC γ′ phase significantly improves mechanical properties, thermal stability, and coarsening resistance.
item.limitations: The tensile strength is lower than Inconel 718 due to the coarsening of the microstructure caused by high-temperature deposition, and the grain size distribution is uneven due to variations in processing parameters and cooling rates.
item.future_work: Post-processing treatments like heat treatment are expected to refine the phase size and improve mechanical properties; precise phase analysis and post-treatment procedures should be added to further advance the manufacturing method.
quotes: The γ′ phase with an ordered FCC structure significantly improves the mechanical properties.
The Ni-Co-Fe-Cr-Al-Ti HEA exhibited a single solid solution with an FCC structure with an average particle size of 116 μm.
The developed HEA exhibited a consistent hardness of approximately 370 HV, showing no variation with height.

records.text: Paper card. Question: Can a Ni-Co-Fe-Cr-Al-Ti high-entropy alloy be manufactured via Directed Energy Deposition (DED) to achieve a γ + γ′ phase structure that enhances thermal stability, coarsening resistance, and strength compared to typical FCC-structured HEAs?. System: Ni-Co-Fe-Cr-Al-Ti HEA (45.0 at% Ni, 20.0 at% Co, 10.0 at% Fe, 10.0 at% Cr, 7.5 at% Al, 7.5 at% Ti) deposited on SUS 304 substrates. Processing: Direct Energy Deposition (DED) using a 2 kW diode laser (980 nm, 3 mm beam diameter) with a laser velocity of 10 mm/s, powder feed rate of 7 g/min, hatch spacing of 1 mm, and 11 layers; powders (45 and 150 μm) mixed for 4 hours; nitrogen carrier gas used to prevent oxidation. Test conditions: Room temperature (20 °C) tensile testing per ASTM E8/E8M-18 standard on specimens with 4.5 mm thickness; microhardness measured via Vickers tester with 5 readings per height; XRD (Cu radiation, 40 kV, 50 mA) and EBSD analysis performed. Findings: The alloy exhibited a γ + γ′ phase structure with an ordered FCC (L12) γ′ phase confirmed by XRD superlattice peaks.; Yield strength was measured at 514 MPa and ultimate tensile strength at 605 MPa (631 MPa in conclusions).; Microhardness was consistent at approximately 370 HV across the deposited height.; The average grain size of the γ phase was coarse, measured at 116 μm.; The γ′ phase composition was identified as (Ni, Co)3(Ti, Al) via EDS analysis.; No secondary precipitated phases other than γ + γ′ were detected in the microstructure.; The hardness exceeded that of wrought Inconel 718 (350 HV).. Mechanism: The addition of aluminum and titanium creates a γ + γ′ phase structure within the multicomponent FCC-HEA matrix, where the ordered FCC γ′ phase significantly improves mechanical properties, thermal stability, and coarsening resistance.. Limitations: The tensile strength is lower than Inconel 718 due to the coarsening of the microstructure caused by high-temperature deposition, and the grain size distribution is uneven due to variations in processing parameters and cooling rates.. Future work: Post-processing treatments like heat treatment are expected to refine the phase size and improve mechanical properties; precise phase analysis and post-treatment procedures should be added to further advance the manufacturing method..
